# PART 1 — UNIVERSAL

These apply to every sdd-micro project regardless of language or
platform. They are deliberately short — this is not the full
hexagonal-architecture / observability / containerization rule set from
the bigger SDD packs (see WHY-SDD.md for why).

## Code Quality

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Config | No hardcoded secrets or credentials — env vars or a gitignored config file |
| Dead code | Delete — never comment out |
| Scope | One task = one concern — don't fold unrelated changes into a task |

## Testing

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Verification | Every task's change is actually run/checked before marking it Done — never assume it passed |
| Kind | Whatever fits the project size: an automated test, a manual run + eyeballed output, or a one-line sanity check — pick the cheapest thing that actually proves it works |

## Git (only if the project uses git)

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Commit | One commit per task, message states what the task did |
| Secrets | Never commit `.env`, credentials, or API keys |

## SDD Workflow

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Order | SPECIFY → [GATE-1] → TASK → IMPLEMENT |
| Gates | GATE-1 (Part 2 confirmed) before /task · tasks.md reviewed before /implement |
| Change | If scope grows mid-project, update tasks.md (or re-run /specify) before writing more code — never code first |
